decisions.reason: As a core cardboard display with some differentiation through adjustability, it is still relatively cheap to offer and worth keeping unless sales have clearly disappointed.
The pegboard-back version fits the firm's existing design and production system and remains a low-cost, somewhat distinctive option in the core range.
After several years, this more standard quarter-pallet concept likely reveals limited incremental value versus overlapping cardboard variants, so resources are better redeployed.
The eighth-pallet format extends the display portfolio in a useful way while staying close to established capabilities, so its option value still outweighs its carrying cost.
Because the wooden pallet is farther from the paper-based core and likely costlier to support, the firm would now be more inclined to exit and focus on core displays and new development.
